correctness.rationale: Perron–Frobenius positivity makes the leading eigenvector of each 9r repeated profile invariant under rotation by nine sites, so eigenvalues reduce to Λ_s(t) for the nine-cycle with t=d/g. Both Λ_s lie strictly in (4/9,1) and decrease with t. Independently used a new SymPy continuant implementation to reproduce exact polynomial difference P_A(z,t)−P_B(z,t)=t⁴(2t+z)(t²−4t−2z+1), and independently computed the two integer-vector Rayleigh quotients 474/941 at t4 and 62/101 at t1. A common top root z must equal q(t)=(t²−4t+1)/2. For 0<t≤4, q(t)≤1/2<Λ_B(4)≤Λ_B(t); for t≥4, q strictly increases and Λ_B strictly decreases, so only one t in (4,5) solves q=Λ_B. Weyl bounds on λ2(A) (<1−2t/5) plus Rayleigh lower bounds on Λ_B at t1 and t5 make sign of P_A(Λ_B) determine sign of Λ_B−Λ_A at both sample points; identities yield opposite signs. Continuous curves with only one possible crossing give the entire t>0 ordering. This proof is global analytic, not extrapolated from finite sampled t.
residual_risks: Rayleigh witnesses and polynomial cancellation are independently exact; proof of second-eigenvalue gap and Perron monotonicity is analytic, not fully machine-certified.

value.rationale: The two landscapes are ecologically natural matched comparisons—same area, number of patches and edge interfaces, differing only favorable run-length balance. The exact unique reversal establishes why these conventional fragmentation statistics cannot impose a universal growth order, a substantive structural counterexample with exact transition, not an arbitrary narrow numerical optimization.
residual_risks: The theorem is only for two nine-site profiles and their repeats, not all spatial arrangements or nonlinear population persistence.

limitations: All results refer to one fixed deterministic linear nearest-neighbor cycle model and any integer number of full repetitions; no nonlinear ecological survival claim.
The exact crossing is characterized implicitly by Λ_B(t)=q(t); quoted decimal is approximate.
